req.title: AWSI - ETP Solutions Architect (full-time)
req.source: Recruiter email screenshots and role brief supplied by the user. Interview scheduling details remain unresolved.

event.location: USC, Los Angeles, in person if selected; room unconfirmed
event.note: The Wednesday hold remains tentative and the email has conflicting date/time wording. Leave this blank until clarified. Enter a confirmed time converted to Pacific Time (America/Los_Angeles); the input does not interpret CST or another time zone.

plan_note: Default: 3 hours per day for 14 days. On a busy day, complete the two Minimum blocks (90 minutes); add the remaining blocks when time permits. Readiness gates are self-assessment targets, not hiring predictions. If a gate is missed, use the next day's extension blocks to repair it.
structure_note: These are preparation scenarios for skills relevant to a Solutions Architect role. They do not claim a particular number, sequence, length, or format of Amazon interviews. Confirm your actual process with the recruiter.

stages.title: Behavioral and resume practice
stages.note: Practice format only. The assessment is passed, but individual interview rounds, duration, and format are not confirmed. In-person USC interviews are conditional on selection.

checklist.text: Reconcile every story claim with the resume and your own evidence; label estimates and missing details.
Record a 60-second introduction and six different two-minute STAR answers with clear personal ownership.
Prepare real failure, disagreement, and mentoring examples; leave gaps visible until verified.
Answer follow-ups about measurement, alternatives, customer impact, and what you would change.

stages.title: AWS architecture practice
stages.note: Use scenarios to practise reasoning, service tradeoffs, and customer requirements. These are not scheduled interview stages.

checklist.text: Draw a secure multi-AZ application and explain the request path, IAM, encryption, logs, and failure handling.
Choose compute, storage, database, and integration services from requirements and explain rejected alternatives.
Explain RTO/RPO, backups versus availability, and cost drivers using a worked scenario.
Complete one unseen design in 30 minutes, including security, scaling, observability, and cost.

stages.title: Customer communication practice
stages.note: Practise discovery before recommendations and adapt technical depth to the audience.

checklist.text: Run two customer role-plays: ask about goals, workload, constraints, risk, budget, and success measures.
Explain one architecture to a business stakeholder in plain language and close with a small next step.
Prepare two informed questions for interviewers and a concise answer to why Amazon and why Solutions Architect.
Confirm actual interview format, date, time zone, and remote or onsite logistics with the recruiter.

plan.deliverable: One introduction, a claim-verification list, two baseline recordings, and a ranked weakness list.
plan.readiness_gate: Explain your own contribution without inventing details; identify three technical weaknesses to revisit.

tasks.text: Audit the resume and story review: mark supported claims, missing ownership, and metrics needing verification. Draft a 60-second SA introduction.
Without notes, explain a web request through DNS, TLS, load balancer, app, and database. Read the AWS priority cheat sheet and mark weak areas.
Record two current STAR answers and score specificity, personal action, results, and follow-up depth.
Create a personal error log and practise Region versus AZ, shared responsibility, and the six Well-Architected pillars.

plan.deliverable: One two-minute story plus a labelled network diagram and troubleshooting notes.
plan.readiness_gate: Correctly trace inbound and outbound traffic and distinguish availability from security.

tasks.text: Rewrite one customer-impact story with a concrete setting, your decision, and an honestly supported result; rehearse it twice.
Draw a VPC with two AZs, public/private subnets, routes, internet and NAT gateways, security groups, and endpoints. Explain the packet path.
Contrast security groups and network ACLs; explain Route 53, CloudFront, ALB, and NLB with one choice each.
Solve a connectivity failure aloud, then answer probes on the story metric and rejected alternative.

plan.focus: Security and the hardest story gaps
plan.deliverable: Two honest gap-story outlines and a least-privilege access flow.
plan.readiness_gate: Explain who can assume a role, which resource it can access, and how you would audit the access.

tasks.text: Draft a real failure or disagreement story. Name your mistake or opposing view, the evidence, and the change you made; retain blanks for unknown facts.
Practise IAM roles and policies, least privilege, STS, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudTrail, and shared responsibility in a workload scenario.
Draft a second real gap example; map both to relevant Leadership Principles without forcing coverage.
Review encryption in transit/at rest, S3 access controls, WAF, and incident detection; remediate your weakest security explanation.

plan.deliverable: A timed application diagram and a compute decision table in your notes.
plan.readiness_gate: Justify your compute choice from requirements and describe what happens when an AZ fails.

tasks.text: Rehearse one ownership story with three explicit personal actions and a decision under constraint.
Design a basic scalable web app. Compare EC2, Auto Scaling, ECS/Fargate, and Lambda against traffic, runtime, operations, and cost needs.
Draw the same design in 30 minutes; add deployment, health checks, scaling signals, and logs.
Use retrieval practice to explain EC2 versus containers versus Lambda; record two tradeoffs you initially missed.

plan.deliverable: A storage/database choice matrix and a two-minute deep-dive answer.
plan.readiness_gate: Distinguish backup, high availability, and read scaling; justify relational versus key-value storage.

tasks.text: Practise a technical deep-dive story: baseline, investigation, alternatives, personal implementation, and how the result was measured.
Choose S3, EBS, EFS, RDS/Aurora, or DynamoDB for sample access patterns. Explain durability, consistency, transactions, and scaling needs.
Compare RDS Multi-AZ and read replicas; add backups, restore tests, and caching to yesterday's design.
Explain lifecycle policies, S3 versioning, ElastiCache, partition keys, and hot partitions without notes.

plan.deliverable: One recorded mock, an honest rubric score, and two improved answers.
plan.readiness_gate: Name your highest-risk behavioral and technical gaps and demonstrate a better answer for each.

tasks.text: Run a 45-minute practice mock: two behavioral prompts and one architecture or technical discussion; record it.
Review the recording and fix the two biggest weaknesses. Re-answer the same prompts with evidence, tradeoffs, and customer outcomes.
Practise queue-based decoupling with SQS, SNS, EventBridge, retries, idempotency, and dead-letter queues.
Review the error log and retest five missed service choices using the cheat sheet only after answering.

plan.deliverable: Three recordings, one unseen diagram, and a focused week-two repair list.
plan.readiness_gate: Answer at least 8 of 10 core service decisions with reasons; produce three complete honest STAR answers. If short, swap day-eight extension blocks for repair.

tasks.text: Record three randomly selected STAR answers; include a failure/disagreement and defend every metric or qualify it clearly.
Draw an unseen web workload in 30 minutes and explain security, AZ failure, scaling, monitoring, and cost in the remaining time.
Repair the weakest story, including a vivid setting, your constraint, turning point, and result; avoid memorizing a script.
Retest core service comparisons from memory and select the two topics that need extra time in week two.

plan.deliverable: A migration plan with rollback, DR objectives, and a cost-driver list.
plan.readiness_gate: Connect recovery choices to business loss and explain why the cheapest architecture may miss the requirement.

tasks.text: Build a migration recommendation: discover dependencies, choose a migration strategy, pilot, validate, and plan rollback.
Choose RTO/RPO and a disaster-recovery approach for a sample business. Explain regional failure, backups, replication, and a restore test.
Rehearse a prioritization or frugality story with the business tradeoff and what you chose not to build.
Estimate major cost drivers, including compute, storage, requests, data transfer, and NAT; explain a cost-reduction plan.

plan.deliverable: A discovery checklist, two audience-specific explanations, and two interviewer questions.
plan.readiness_gate: Restate the customer problem before naming a service and close with an agreed next step and success measure.

tasks.text: Run a customer role-play: clarify the business goal, audience, workload, constraints, risk, and success criteria before recommending.
Explain your recommendation to a business stakeholder in two minutes, then to an engineer with a diagram and explicit tradeoffs.
Rehearse a disagreement story with respectful challenge, evidence, the final decision, and how you committed afterward.
Practise why Amazon, why SA, and two interviewer questions grounded in the role.

plan.deliverable: One event-driven diagram with failure paths and one incident story recording.
plan.readiness_gate: Explain duplicate delivery, retry limits, idempotency, and how an operator detects and repairs failure.

tasks.text: Design an event-driven document or order workflow with retries, duplicate handling, DLQ, and user-visible status.
Explain API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, Step Functions, CloudWatch, and CloudTrail through that workflow; identify failure and cost risks.
Rehearse an incident or dive-deep story, including signals, hypotheses, isolation, recovery, and prevention.
Review deployment rollback, infrastructure as code, tracing, alarms, and runbooks; correct your weakest operations answer.

plan.deliverable: An honest project deep dive and a RAG diagram with evaluation and access controls.
plan.readiness_gate: Separate your actual experience from a proposed AWS mapping and name measurable quality and safety checks.

tasks.text: Explain one real AI/data project from the resume: problem, your contribution, evaluation, limitations, and what was actually deployed.
Sketch a RAG workload with S3, retrieval, Bedrock, identity, citations, evaluation, and data access controls. Explain when simpler search is enough.
Review Bedrock versus SageMaker AI and Athena versus Redshift versus streaming services at a decision level.
Probe hallucinations, prompt injection, sensitive data, latency, and inference cost; connect mitigations to requirements.

plan.deliverable: A scored second mock, two repaired answers, and a revised architecture.
plan.readiness_gate: Give six distinct STAR answers without unsupported claims and defend the key design tradeoffs.

tasks.text: Run a 45-minute mock with a friend if available; otherwise record yourself with unseen prompts and no answer notes.
Review for vague context, unsupported results, missing personal decisions, service-name dumping, and absent customer discovery. Repair two answers.
Repeat the weakest architecture under a 30-minute timer and explain a cheaper or simpler alternative.
Retest missed AWS comparisons and prepare follow-up answers for six core stories.

plan.deliverable: A readiness scorecard, ten service-choice answers, and a short remaining-gaps list.
plan.readiness_gate: Target 8/10 justified service choices, six defensible stories, and a complete 30-minute design. Unmet gates become the only final-day study topics.

tasks.text: Record a mini panel: introduction, two different LP stories, one resume drill-down, and why SA. Focus on clarity and follow-ups.
Retest ten priority AWS decisions and explain a secure multi-AZ workload plus one recovery strategy from a blank page.
Use the story review to fix the lowest-scoring remaining answer and update your evidence notes.
Rehearse one customer scenario and verify interview date, time zone, format, tools, and recruiter instructions if supplied.

plan.deliverable: A personal recall sheet, final gap list, and confirmed logistics where available.
plan.readiness_gate: Know which claims you can defend, which gaps remain, and how to reason aloud when you do not know. This is a preparation checkpoint, not an assumed interview date.

tasks.text: Rehearse the introduction and three weakest story openings, then answer their hardest follow-up questions without scripts.
Use the cheat sheet for active recall of remaining priority gaps; redraw one architecture and narrate the customer outcome.
Review the error log and readiness gates. Create a one-page personal recall sheet with story hooks and service tradeoffs.
Prepare interview logistics only if confirmed; practise a calm close and next steps, then stop early enough to rest.

logistics: Clarify the tentative Wednesday hold and conflicting weekday/date and CST/local wording with the recruiter. Confirm the actual date, start time and time zone before entering a Pacific time here.
For remote interviews, test audio, camera, connection, and the requested drawing tool; for onsite interviews, confirm the location and arrival instructions.
Keep your resume, a notebook, story hooks, and interviewer questions ready; follow recruiter guidance about permitted materials.
Protect sleep and arrive or connect with enough buffer. The 14-day plan can finish before or after a date you enter; adjust it deliberately.

role.cohort_note: Planned cohort starts from the role brief; the candidate choice is unknown. These are employment start options, not interview dates.
focus: Design customer solutions and explain architecture choices against customer requirements.
Collaborate with sales and adapt communication from engineers to executives.
Connect technical recommendations to measurable positive customer outcomes.
role.success: The role brief frames success through positive customer impact, not sales quotas.

recruiting_context.plan_relationship: Keep the October 15 to October 28 preparation window until the actual interview timing is clarified. Day 14 is a readiness checkpoint. A tentative Wednesday hold does not automatically move or shorten the study plan.
